title: Missing baby rescued after being buried alive in a dog crate in South Carolina
summary: A missing 11-month-old infant was rescued Tuesday after being buried alive in a dog crate in South Carolina.

image.caption: In a photo supplied by his great aunt, 11-month-old Koah Sharp is seen sleeping Nov. 7, days before being buried alive. (Amber Hammond/Handout/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
A missing 11-month-old infant was rescued Tuesday after being buried alive in a dog crate in South Carolina.
Searchers found the infant wrapped in a towel about 24 hours after he was reported missing

A county sheriff says little Koah Sharp had been underground for about 24 hours but survived, likely due to an air pocket created by a towel wrapped around the crate. Cool temperatures may also have helped.
Dozens of first responders combed the countryside for the "bright boy with reddish blond hair" that the sheriff's office said had disappeared while his grandmother ran errands.

After a full day of searching, authorities found freshly disturbed soil in the woods not far from the home of the boy's grandfather. They began digging and soon unearthed the baby, who was "clinging to life," the sheriff said.

"Certainly, God is good," Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference, not long after Koah was found. "He was screaming at the top of his lungs, which is a good thing in the baby world, I would guess."

A photo provided by the Lexington County Sheriff's office in Lexington, S.C., shows Michael Comer in custody after his son was found buried alive. (Lexington County Sheriff's Office/The Associated Press)
The child's father, Michael Comer, 25, was arrested and was being held without bond on a burglary charge, Koon said. Investigators were working with prosecutors to confirm further charges, he said.
Koah, who disappeared Monday in the county just west of Columbia, was taken to a hospital. His condition was not immediately known Wednesday.
"We're better now that we know that Koah is safe," his great aunt, Amber Hammond, told The Associated Press in an interview. She was watching as he was freed from the crate.
100 people helped in search
Deputies who searched the grandfather's home found the doors open and baby belongings inside, but they did not see Comer or the child, the sheriff said. Then the digging started.
"It was shallow," Koon said. "It was probably about at least a foot from the top of that crate to the top of the ground."
It was not immediately known if Comer had a lawyer. A phone number could not be found for him. The Associated Press sent emails seeking information to the public defender and prosecutors.
Nearly 100 first responders participated in the search.
Authorities said Koah had been in the care of Comer's mother. She had to run an errand and left the boy in Comer's care. Another caregiver was on the way, Koon said.
"By the time the caregiver got there, Michael was gone, and Koah was gone with him," Koon said.

blocks.text: Surveillance video from several businesses in the area showed Comer without the infant on Monday afternoon, Koon said. The father was found Monday night and was arrested.
Koah's parents "have had some situations" regarding domestic violence charges, the sheriff said.
"Children," he said, "sometimes get caught in the middle."

Comer was sentenced to probation in October after pleading guilty to domestic violence and aggravated breach-of-peace charges related to an arrest in July, Lexington County online court records show. Prosecutors dropped a gun charge as part of the plea deal.
